name: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve
blurb: Caribou, wolves and tundra in a roadless Brooks Range wilderness.

tip.title: Remove the caribou
tip.text: Caribou feed wolves, bears and scavengers. Set Caribou to -100% and watch the wolf, grizzly, wolverine and raven, while lichen is left ungrazed.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Gates of the Arctic National Park and Preserve
National Park Service: Gates of the Arctic nature and science

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Midnight sun and short summer
nodes.desc: Above the Arctic Circle the summer sun barely sets, so plants race through a short growing season before long dark winters.

nodes.name: Snow and snowfields
nodes.desc: Snow insulates the ground in winter and its meltwater wets the tundra in spring. Perennial snowfields in the Brooks Range have shrunk a great deal since 1985.

nodes.name: Permafrost
nodes.desc: Frozen ground lies just below a thin thawed surface layer. Warming has begun to thaw it, causing erosion and slope failures.

nodes.name: Thin tundra soil
nodes.desc: Cold, shallow soils hold limited nutrients that plants and decomposers recycle slowly.

nodes.name: Fungi and soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and carcasses, slowly in the cold, and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Sedges
nodes.desc: Grass-like plants that form much of the tundra and wet meadow cover. GloBI records caribou eating water sedge.

nodes.name: Arctic willows
nodes.desc: Low shrubby willows of the tundra and river valleys. Willow ptarmigan are recorded eating grayleaf willow.

nodes.name: Cowberry and heath shrubs
nodes.desc: Low evergreen shrub with tart berries. GloBI records it eaten by caribou, ptarmigan, longspurs, foxes and ravens.

nodes.name: Reindeer lichens
nodes.desc: A pale ground lichen. Wikipedia says caribou dig through snow to reach it, and it is a winter staple for them.

nodes.name: Caribou
nodes.desc: Wikipedia describes migrations between taiga winter range and tundra summer range. The Western Arctic herd moves through the central Brooks Range and feeds wolves, bears and people.

nodes.name: Dall sheep
nodes.desc: A white mountain sheep of alpine slopes in the Brooks Range that grazes grasses and sedges.

nodes.name: Tundra vole
nodes.desc: A small rodent of wet tundra and a well-recorded species here. It eats sedges and other plants, and is prey for foxes, stoats and wolves.

nodes.name: Brown lemming
nodes.desc: A tundra rodent that eats sedges and other plants and is a common prey of foxes and stoats.

nodes.name: Arctic ground squirrel
nodes.desc: Eats plants and some small animals, then hibernates through winter. GloBI records it as prey of grizzlies and wolverines.

nodes.name: Willow ptarmigan
nodes.desc: A grouse that feeds on willow buds and twigs and other tundra plants. GloBI records it as prey of foxes, wolverines, grizzlies and stoats.

nodes.name: Lapland longspur
nodes.desc: A tundra songbird that eats seeds and plants and, in summer, insects. A very commonly recorded bird here.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: A small weasel that hunts voles, lemmings and birds. GloBI records both foxes and wolves eating it.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Eats rodents, birds and berries. GloBI records it feeding on voles, lemmings, ptarmigan and caribou.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A scavenging bird that feeds on carrion, berries and small animals, and stays all winter in the Arctic.

nodes.name: Wolverine
nodes.desc: A strong scavenger and predator. GloBI records it eating caribou, ground squirrels, ptarmigan and voles.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Hunts caribou, Dall sheep and smaller animals in the Brooks Range. A top predator of the caribou herds.

nodes.name: Grizzly bear
nodes.desc: The park has a low density of grizzlies, roughly one bear per 100 square miles. They eat berries, ground squirrels and caribou.
